validation.reason_not_fully_accepted: The degree-2 three-phase junction has only one attached compatible branch; 260–274 bara also remains unresolved.
validation.repository_default_suite_note: The 20-minute run did not finish. Two reproducible FieldFluidRunner contract mismatches and one independent CompressorTest numerical mismatch were observed; none of these source or test files was edited by this six-item topology task.

approach: Kept the exact SRK/Peneloux/classic model frozen; reran 882 independent cold-start TP flashes; built strict zero-TPD fixed-pressure anchor ledgers; applied global-stability gates and bidirectional pseudo-arclength continuation; solved the GO→GOW junction with coupled simultaneous-incidence equations; and replayed the product audit after removing overlapping restart assembly.
conclusions: The TPflash mainline remains fully operational on the 882-state sampled grid. The GO→GOW main branch is verified through its physical three-phase point at 229.9322 bara, and a distinct OW→GOW branch is verified from 284 to 300 bara. The complete 200–300 bara network is not closed because the compatible branch at the degree-2 three-phase junction is absent and the 260–274 bara candidate root cluster remains unresolved. The product correctly reports VERIFIED_BRANCHES_INCOMPLETE_NETWORK rather than promoting a partial envelope.

figure_discussion.title: Main branch and endpoint
figure_discussion.observation: Nine fixed-pressure roots agree with continuation within 0.0825 K; the coupled endpoint is 229.9322 bara and 313.4988 °C.
figure_discussion.mechanism: As beta tends to one, oil and aqueous phases are simultaneously incipient from the gas mother phase; a minimum arc step occurs just before the physical junction.
figure_discussion.implication: The numerical continuation stop is not the endpoint, but the corrected main branch is physically closed at the coupled three-phase point.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Use the coupled endpoint in the product network and retain the degree-2 attachment requirement.

figure_discussion.title: Second branch with segmented trust
figure_discussion.observation: Eight fixed-pressure roots verify 284–300 bara and agree with continuation within 0.0846 K.
figure_discussion.mechanism: This branch represents gas appearing from an oil-water mother state; below about 274 bara the retained oil stability mode rejects the continued root.
figure_discussion.implication: A second physical boundary exists, but isolated 260/262 roots cannot be joined across the rejected interval.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Use 284–300 bara as verified boundary evidence; keep 260–274 bara limited/unresolved.

figure_discussion.title: Old phase switches versus strict envelope
figure_discussion.observation: The old TPflash switch inventory contains multiple high-pressure transitions at one pressure, while the strict audit retains two verified branch segments and one continuation-only extension.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Surface phase-count changes can be displaced or contaminated by duplicate phase families; zero-TPD correction and global stability distinguish physical boundaries from map artifacts.
figure_discussion.implication: A converged TPflash grid proves state-solving robustness but does not by itself prove a closed phase-envelope topology.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Expose product trustStatus and branch-level quality; do not promote the complete 200–300 bara envelope until the missing compatible branch is attached.
